best_for: Linux, Windows and Mac users who want a free, Paint.NET-style editor with layers and effects for quick photo fixes, diagrams and pixel art, without learning GIMP.
description:
Pinta is a drawing and image editor written in C# with GTK. Jonathan Pobst started it in 2010, and the Pinta community builds it today.

You can switch between a dark and a light look from the View menu. A canvas grid with a size you choose helps with pixel art, and a nearest-neighbor option keeps hard pixel edges when you resize. Effects include Dithering, Voronoi Diagram, Vignette, Dents and outlines around objects. Offset Selection grows or shrinks the current selection. The [ and ] keys change brush size and line width for many tools, and add-ins can extend the app.

points.title: Paint.NET, rebuilt for every desktop
points.text: Pinta began as a GTK clone of Paint.NET 3.0 and still feels like it: select, crop, resize, clone, recolor and magic wand sit where Windows users expect them. It runs on Linux, Windows, macOS and BSD.

points.title: Layers, effects and unlimited undo
points.text: You get layers with blend modes, a wide set of adjustments and effects with live previews, and an undo history with no fixed limit. Version 3.1 added a polygon lasso, a Cells effect and handles for adjusting gradients on the canvas.

points.title: Free under the MIT license
points.text: There is no paid tier, no account and no store. The code is MIT-licensed, with parts taken from Paint.NET 3.36 under the same license.

points.title: Single-layer formats get flattened
points.text: Saving a layered image as PNG or JPEG flattens it, and Pinta warns you first. Keep a copy in a format that stores layers if you plan to edit them again.

points.title: Screenshot command missing on Windows
points.text: Since the move to GTK4 in Pinta 3.0, File > New Screenshot calls the system screenshot tool on Linux and macOS. The release notes say it is not supported on Windows.

points.title: Builds for Arm and Intel alike
points.text: Windows installers come in x64 and Arm64 for one user or all users. macOS has separate Intel and Apple silicon disk images. The Linux Flatpak is verified on Flathub as published by the project, for x64 and Arm64.

points.title: Older versions mostly on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 10 versions. macOS and Linux list only the current release, so going back there means the project's GitHub releases page.
